events.text: HM Land Registry confirmed our 20 October 2026 email is being handled as EIR request F261029 and FOI request F261030, with a statutory reply deadline of 17 November 2026.

We confirm the internal review into the family's Freedom of Information request about Ty Mawr / Great House Farm records (ref CAS-356384-B2F5L9) is still ongoing, with a final decision expected by 20 November 2026.

We are not aware of any outstanding or live claim against BP or related entities over Great House Farm, noting the matter was settled by the 1987 Court of Appeal decision, so we cannot confirm a preservation hold without a specific claim being set out. We also ask for documents in PDF or Word as the links sent are inaccessible.
We acknowledge your information request, now reference IR1038, and will reply substantively in due course under FOIA, the section 45 Code of Practice and data protection law.

We confirm Bute X.6(12) is still held here but found no information about the property; our manuscript index showed no matches. Scanning would need to go through Glamorgan Archives at a cost, and detailed research would also carry a charge once assessed; an in-person visit is also possible.

HM Land Registry told us the matter under enquiry 260928-6762800 and N610CGV has been referred to one of its lawyers, which will delay a reply, with no further detail given.

Under ref 2026/4460 we confirm occurrence books end in 1984 and station logs in 1979; the 1988 Weekly Orders exist but are closed as they name serving officers, though a paid search can be commissioned; we hold no press-office files for the period.

Under ref 2026/4461, we confirm our holdings are designated for permanent preservation and will not be destroyed; we hold no planning files but do hold Planning Committee papers DCVG/C/4/36/76-77 and DCVG/C/4/36/94 for applications 1989/01396/OUT and 1992/00671/RES.

We acknowledged receipt on 16 October 2026 of your request for corporate business records, gave it reference CAS-361652-D3X8X9, and confirmed we will respond by 13 November 2026 under the 20 working-day rule in section 10.
We explained that the Library does not engage with AI agents, so we could not respond to this enquiry about the Bute Estate records for Great House Farm.

We confirm the 11 October decision was an officer assessment of the proposal as submitted, not a formal Committee decision, and say a separate proposal on records management and access to historic planning information could be considered through our normal work programming process, though it would not review individual cases.
We confirm receipt of your correspondence and explain how we handle new complaints, updates to existing cases, and advice requests, including timescales and tribunal appeal rights if we delay.
We give you the case reference IC-586450-N8N0 for your complaint and explain you can add further relevant information by replying or emailing with that reference.
We confirm this was an old file from our London office, which closed in 1996, and that no records from it remain in storage.
We give you the reference number FOIR26#25631/1 for the request about Western Ground Rents Ltd.
The family channel posted a video.
The family’s Instagram carousel set four plans of the farm side by side, from the 1824 Bute estate survey to the May 1939 agreement plan.
The family’s Instagram reel explained the 1841 tithe apportionment: the Marquess of Bute as landowner, John Williams as occupier, 36 parcels of about 119 acres.
The family’s Instagram carousel listed six kinds of record behind the farm’s story, from the 1881 census to the 1987 law report.

We ask for an internal review of case 00211463 after no response arrived by the 19 October 2026 deadline, repeating requests for the 89/01396/OUT planning file appendices, Policy H.2 text, and a held/not held answer with search details for each item.

I accept your preservation answer under ref 2026/4461 and ask four follow-up points: whether DCVG/C/4/36/76-77 includes its appendices and its access status, what was searched, any pre-1974 planning or land charges registers, and whether ref 2026/4439's collection also covers the 1877 division or 1938 conveyance.

I asked for the location only of any closed or open records on Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, covering OS Glamorgan XLVII.6, including IR 58 field books and plans, with series/piece references, open or closed status, and confirmation of a physical check before any viewing or copying.

The family confirms they want records only on the c.1880 ironwork find at Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, listing variant names to search, and asks for a section 16 cost-limit steer if needed.

I confirm I understand the 11 October reply was an officer assessment, not a Committee decision, and that any new scrutiny topic goes through normal work programming. I now formally propose a county-wide topic titled 'Management of, and public access to, historic planning, land-charges and heritage records', with four scope points covering record transfers since 1996, search practices, request handling, and possible improvements.

I lodge a section 50 complaint against the Ministry of Justice over request 260813002 on 1988-1989 court files, arguing the 9 October 2026 internal review gave no description of any search and failed to address items 7 and 8 on retention and disposal records.

I chased two unanswered questions from 26 August about which coroner's jurisdiction covered Llandough Hospital in 1983 and where its registers went, and whether a 1990 referral for the other death could be found in the system already searched, asking the office to forward this to the Council's FOI team if needed or treat it as a review request.

We asked Historic England, under EIR regulation 11, to reconsider three points in its 21 October reply (ref 26/04323): whether any record of the 12 January 2018 microfiche transfer survives, who authorised it and why, and whether any copy or index was kept afterwards.

We describe DBDT/123/7, a 1939 tenancy agreement for 5.30 acres next to Tŷ Mawr farmhouse, which does not mention the farmhouse and reserves quarrying rights; we hold no later title history and suggest a land-law specialist, also flagging the 1936 Llwyn-yr-eryr sale particulars in DSA/14/91.

We reply as one response to your further emails: Cadw has no separate complaints process, the Complaints Advice Team already said it cannot investigate, and we have nothing further to add without contemporary evidence; information under FOI/EIR requests will not be destroyed, and we see no merit in continuing to correspond.

We have considered request 1189/26 and attach our response, setting out the section 8 tests for a valid request; you may ask for a review and then complain to the Information Commissioner if still dissatisfied.
We confirm receipt of your internal review correspondence on FOI 719/26 (1188/26) and note that a backlog may delay our response beyond 20 working days.
We confirm receipt of your correspondence on FOI 1040/26 and note that a current backlog may delay our response beyond the usual 20 working days.
We confirm receipt of your correspondence on FOI 1189/26 and note that a current backlog may delay our response beyond the usual 20 working days.
I confirm I have received your request for a referral to the Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman regarding the HM Land Registry complaint, case ref KN806, and have logged it for a response.
We confirm automatic receipt of the family's email in our Subject Access Request mailbox and will respond once reviewed.
We confirm receipt of your correspondence and explain how we handle new complaints, updates to existing cases, and advice requests, including timescales and tribunal appeal rights if we delay.

We hold five metadata records and digital resources on Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr, including Coflein, Glamorgan-Gwent HER entries covering the 1990 excavation and demolition, and the 1994 Cotswold Archaeology publication and dataset.

We explain that CPS cannot accept or consider information sent directly by the public, that we have no knowledge of the referenced case, and we direct you to report any concerns to the police instead.
We respond to request FOI2026/23886 on 1936–1955 Great House Farm records; our search of paper and electronic records found the information is not held, though it may be held by the Welsh Government.

We confirm receipt of the 20 October request about Western Ground Rents Ltd and tell you we are considering it under the Freedom of Information Act 2000, with a reply to follow within 20 working days.
We confirm, on the reviewer's instruction, that her decision not to investigate further is final.

Under EIR regulation 12(4)(a) we said we hold no information matching the request, but noted that archaeological report microfiches, including any Welsh material, were transferred to RCAHMW on 12 January 2018.

We follow up on FOI/EIR requests 00211483 and 00211484, noting the 16 October 2026 deadline passed with no reply or extension notice, ask for confirmation and a reference for the 18 October supplement, and request record preservation; we may complain to the ICO after 4 November 2026.

I told HM Land Registry that subject access request 260928-6762800 is bound by the statutory one-month deadline of 28 October 2026, not service standards, and asked for written confirmation on logging, timing, preservation of files, and the status of enquiry 260918-6720625.

I thank you for ref 2026/4439 and ask follow-up questions on DSA/14/91's 1936 sale particulars, any head lease for the Spencer land, accession details for DBDT/123, and whether later Leckwith Common and planning papers are held, requesting a reply by 18 November 2026.

Following ref 2026-3769, I correct William Beverly Buckler's death date to 15 May 1992 at Llandough Hospital and ask you to confirm the Llandough register covers through 1992 and March 1983 for Mary Doreen Williams, with free look-up if possible.

I ask you to confirm by 4 November 2026 whether your 21 October email is the final response to complaint TO/HF/05677/26 or whether a further stage exists, to explain the policy behind restricting correspondence, and to extend preservation to listed records including the 1988 listing file and inspection photographs.

I accepted the case sequence you gave (CAS-344046, CAS-347296, CAS-356384) and asked you to confirm the date the internal review outcome will be issued, whether my 7 October email was joined to that review, and whether my National Farm Survey/CWAEC query was passed to Records Enquiries under CAS-344046.

I pressed South Wales Police to treat my request as an internal review of FOI 719/26 (ref 1188/26), due 26 October 2026, needing no clarification, and asked for details of searches, retention schedules, destruction records and any transfer to Glamorgan Archives, plus confirmation that records stay preserved pending this review, the subject access request and FOI 1264/26.

I asked South Wales Police to review FOI 1040/26's "not held" answer about two deaths, pointing to the corrected May 1992 death date, a seven-day breach of the statutory deadline, and the lack of any explanation of what was searched or where records might now sit.

I clarified that my 28 September email on FOI 1189/26 was a preservation notice, not an information request, and asked South Wales Police to confirm in writing that records on Great House Farm and the two deaths are held under a hold until all open reviews and requests close, by 4 November 2026.

I set out exactly what my subject access request covers: records naming me in the 1988 possession and demolition, records from handling my later requests (719/26, 1188/26, 1040/26, 1189/26, 1264/26), and the crime-recording decision, and I confirmed the reply is due by 29 October 2026.

Thank you for clarifying that Dinas Powys falls outside your constituency; following your suggestion, the request for a Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman referral over title WA231076 has gone to the MP for Cardiff South and Penarth, and HM Land Registry's Independent Complaints Reviewer is now reviewing it under ref ICR/090/26, so no action is needed from your office.

I set out twelve questions I intend to ask at Thursday's meeting, covering the remote-only decision, notice republication, multi-location arrangements, the status of my pending internal review and narrower records request, and future agenda access.

I ask you to treat this ticket, my 15 October reply and enquiry 9816877 as one enquiry, and ask you to confirm whether the catalogue shows any 1876–77 instrument for the farmhouse or a 1916 tenancy to John Williams.

I accept that archive 6364275 relates to Bonvilston, confirm an order for scans of items 6048945, 6048943 and 6048941, ask for the order form to be resent, and raise three new questions on Cadw records, 1974 survey notes and aerial sortie lists, requesting reply by 18 November 2026.

I ask you to confirm the date and store location of the physical search of the HER source file, clarify whether ironwork finds from 1880, 1979 and 1994 are distinguished in records, and request the file not be weeded while enquiries continue.

I accept a Task and Finish review won't revisit one planning decision, but press for a separate county-wide scrutiny topic on how the Council keeps and discloses historic planning and heritage records, citing the still-overdue EIR 00210772 review and missing appendices C, D and E. I ask who took the 11 October decision, which channels apply, and whether a ward member or complaints route could help.

I confirm the family will sign the application themselves, correct William Buckler's death date to 15 May 1992 at Llandough Hospital, and ask whether any records survive for him or Mary Doreen Williams, with destruction details if not, and that any surviving records be preserved.

I thank the Commissioner for clarifying the limits of their remit and confirm I will submit complaints one request at a time as suggested, listing internal reviews now running for South Wales Police and Welsh Government. I ask four questions: on records management under the section 46 Code, on reporting destruction of material within scope of live requests, and on late responses.

I follow up on FOI2026/23272, asking that any destroyed 1988 records cite the retention rule under JSP 441, that any transfer reference be given, and warn I will seek internal review if no reply arrives by 9 November 2026.

I followed up on internal review IR/26/16, noting a Welsh Government refusal of a related request (ATISN 27589) on 19 October 2026, and asked which files the original 22 September reply meant, what systems were searched, and for preservation of any records while the review and any Information Commissioner complaint remain open.

I accept the CPS's position that evidence is for the police, but ask under FOIA whether the CPS holds or once held any file on the 1988 Great House Farm summons withdrawn in 1989, plus retention records and search details, and treat part of this as a subject access request.

I follow up on the internal review of FOI2026/06174 (ref IR2026/06711), accepting heritage functions passed to Wales in 1984 but disputing that this explains a nil return for post-1988 records, and I ask for search details and predecessor file references by 18 November 2026.

I acknowledge your confirmation and note the statutory deadline of 17 November 2026, ask for a reference number, request preservation of related files, and ask whether any vested property was later disclaimed, sold or dealt with, or if records were destroyed.

The family writes to confirm FOI2026/118465 covers their 20 October request on rating records for Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr, stresses the 17 November deadline is a legal limit under section 10(1), asks for preservation of relevant records, and warns of an internal review and ICO complaint if no response arrives by then.
We confirm receipt of your email and explain that, under our strict rules, we can only take up casework for constituents living in Cardiff South and Penarth.

events.text: We again ask for a claim number to identify your historical case correctly, and point you to the published County Court Records Retention and Disposition Schedule on GOV.uk for information on how records are kept and destroyed.

We confirm the published agenda specifies a remote meeting, that members of the public can request a Zoom link to attend, and that you will be given a reasonable opportunity to ask questions and comment on agenda items.

events.text: Requests clarification on the scope of the ironwork search before proceeding and places the request on hold.
The LGA confirms it is treating your request under the Freedom of Information Act and will respond within the statutory deadline of 17 November 2026.
We confirmed receipt of your enquiry about glebe, exchange and Bute Estate records for Llandough-juxta-Penarth (ECE/6/3/372/CD27551) and said a fuller reply should follow within 10 working days.
My earlier message to Defra could not be delivered because a mail routing loop was detected between the mail systems involved.
We confirm this inbox only handles FOIA/EIR information requests and direct any other correspondence to our webform or postal address instead.
We acknowledged receipt of the request (our reference 26/04323) about Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr and said a full response would follow within the statutory 20 working day period under FOI/EIR.

We confirmed your request, reference FOI-26-46, will now be handled formally under the Freedom of Information Act, and apologised that Customer Services never replied; we will respond by 17 November 2026.
HMRC's Valuation Office sends an automatic acknowledgement confirming receipt of the request and explaining how FOI, EIR and data protection requests are handled, including statutory timescales.
HMRC's Information Rights Unit confirms receipt of the request on 20 October 2026, assigns reference FOI2026/118465, and states it aims to respond within 20 working days by 17 November 2026.

I replied to HM Land Registry's 1 October 2026 email on subject access request D260928 and added a new request under the Environmental Information Regulations and FOIA for first-registration and amalgamation documents concerning WA231076 and WA240304.

I thank your office for forwarding HMLR's reply on 18 September, note the Independent Complaints Reviewer's 9 October refusal (ICR/090/26) and HMLR's new internal application Z084NQV, and ask you to put three factual questions to HMLR's Chief Executive about notice to occupiers before first registration, the missing 1969 conveyance, and the 1987 amalgamation of the titles while the BP Properties v Buckler appeal was pending. I also ask whether the Ministry of Justice has replied, and request referral to the Ombudsman if the Reviewer's decision proves final and HMLR's answers do not resolve matters.

I submit a new, narrower information request about Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), seeking records on village green VG41's 1970 registration, planning applications 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES, correspondence with BP Properties and the Vale of Glamorgan Council, and where pre-2002 council records are now held.

I correct my previous email, explaining it was sent as a reply to the wrong message so an earlier email I'd asked to be disregarded appeared quoted beneath it; I confirm my 20 October request itself still stands unaffected.

I accept the Zoom arrangements for Thursday's meeting without withdrawing my objection to the lack of an in-person option, and restate four unanswered questions about who made the remote-only decision, notice revisions, published multi-location arrangements, and consideration of public access.

I asked the LGA under FOIA for 1965-2000 guidance to councils on disputed land title and village green registration, plus any records mentioning Great House Farm, Western Ground Rents, BP Properties or the 1987 Court of Appeal case, by 17 November 2026.

I asked the WLGA, on a voluntary basis, for records on disputed land title guidance, the 1996 allocation of South Glamorgan land at Llandough and Leckwith between Cardiff and the Vale of Glamorgan, and any mention of Great House Farm or the 1987 case, by 17 November 2026.

I asked Audit Wales under FOIA/EIR for 1970-1996 audit reports, working papers, elector objections and correspondence about council land dealings at Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr, village green VG41 and Church View Close, by 17 November 2026.

I resent my FOI/EIR request about Audit Wales records on council land dealings at Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr after the first email bounced, sending it to the published Freedom of Information address instead.

I asked BT Group Archives for 1950-1990 records on Great House Farm, Llandough, including directory listings, wayleave agreements, the 1988-89 service cessation, and engineering plans, or guidance on Openreach records, by 17 November 2026.

I followed up my preservation notice to Blake Morgan, asking whether it succeeded Robbins Olivey & Blake Lapthorn, whether any 1986-87 case files on Great House Farm survive, and what searches were made, by 17 November 2026.

I asked Lambeth Palace Library for details on file ECE/6/3/372/CD27551 and any related glebe, exchange or Bute Estate records for Llandough-juxta-Penarth, including possible links to the 1879 Lee–Thompson land exchange and Bute Estate correspondence.
The requester asks Defra for MAF-era records on Great House Farm, 1936–1955, covering surveys, committee decisions, consents, compensation and correspondence.
After my first attempt bounced due to a mail routing loop, I resend the same FOI/EIR request about 1936–1955 Great House Farm records to Defra's published GOV.UK address.

I ask the Bona Vacantia Division under FOIA whether any property or interest of the dissolved Western Ground Rents Ltd (company no. 00342092) was referred to or vested in the Crown, especially at Llandough, Leckwith, Cogan or Penarth, and what was done with it.

I ask the reviewer to reconsider, on the limited basis of HM Land Registry's own procedure, three unanswered factual questions about notice to occupiers before 1982–83 registration, the missing 1969 root deed, and the basis for the 1987 amalgamation; if she will not reconsider, I ask for written confirmation that her decision is final so I can pursue an Ombudsman referral.

We asked Historic England under FOI for records on Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, including the 15 January 2018 transfer of archive item 6500905 to RCAHMW, its acquisition history, any retained copies, and related correspondence on its listing and 1988 demolition.

We asked Natural Resources Wales under EIR for the Cwm Cydfin SSSI (site 0524) notification documents, owner and occupier lists from 1972 and 1985, objections and boundary decisions, and records on woodland title WA735527 at Llandough, including its 1994 transfer to Forest of Cardiff and 2005 part-transfer to Goldsworthy Homes.

I followed up as Customer Services never replied, and asked that two specific parts of my original request be treated as a formal FOIA/EIR request: for records of naming and label-placement changes around Ty Mawr/Great House Farm between 1950 and 1975, and for guidance on how such farm names were assigned or altered across editions.

We ask Persimmon Homes to confirm receipt of our 27 September preservation request and to provide records on the 1993 BP transfer, due diligence, title insurance, internal approvals, and the 1994 excavation of human remains at Great House Farm.

The family asks the Valuation Office Agency, under FOIA, for rating and valuation records for Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr from 1955–1995, including ratepayer/owner entries, any disputes or appeals to alter records, and disposal or transfer details, requesting a response by 17 November 2026.
The statutory deadline passed with no reply (ref 00211463).

events.text: We confirm receipt and aim to answer within 20 working days, noting that many enquiries drafted with AI make it harder for staff to identify the relevant request and can delay replies.
We send our disclosure response to ATISN 26-0010 on retention and destruction schedules, noting that some of the requested information may not be specifically recorded.
We confirm receipt of your request of 28 September 2026 and attach our response letter covering Welsh Office/Cadw papers for Great House Farm from the second half of 1988.
We confirm receipt of your consolidated enquiry about Bute Estate Records and related items for Great House Farm, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, and note that replies may be delayed.
The family shared a video in the public Vale of Glamorgan HUB group, linking the dartboard timeline of the case.

Following up on FOI 00211027, I ask for the remaining documents from deed wallet 1756 besides the already-provided 1965 conveyance, including any abstract of title and the 1962 conveyance plan between Western Ground Rents Ltd and Lakeside and Llandough Development Co Ltd.

I ask whether you hold the original South Glamorgan County Council 'County Treasures' inventory from the late 1970s, any entry in it for Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, and related survey material, with a reply requested by 16 November 2026.

I explain I have no claim numbers but list known proceedings for Great House Farm from 1955 to 1988, and ask whether any records survive, were transferred, or were destroyed, also querying the earlier 'no records' reply from 4 August 2026.

I ask for an internal review of ATISN 26-0010, questioning whether any actual record of destruction, transfer or retention exists for the farm's files, which schedule entry was relied on, whether Welsh Office schedules are held, and how searches were conducted.

I consolidated outstanding questions across several cases: exact locations for the Glamorgan XLVII.6 field book, which IR 58 entries match four modern Land Registry titles, records of the 1986-87 possession proceedings, the Bonvilston distinction, and a quotation or page count for the BT 31/87651 company file for Western Ground Rents Ltd.

I ask BP Archive to identify who holds property, litigation and demolition records from 1969–1993 for Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, covering conveyances, title registrations, the 1988 court case and the 1993 transfer, with a reply requested by 16 November 2026.

I combine my outstanding points into one enquiry, asking for a search of Bute Estate Records 1870–1880 for Cedfin/Tŷ Mawr/Great House transactions, items D153/4–8 and D219, and the 1938 conveyance to Western Ground Rents, plus any later records of the farm, requesting a reply by 6 November 2026.
The family asks us to reconcile our 'not held' answers with two published sources stating medieval ironwork from Great House Farm, Llandough, found c.1880, is in the National Museum's collections.

I follow up on your 16 October reply, asking whether searches extended beyond the HER to former GGAT curatorial, project archive and correspondence files, and querying archive-location fields for 1978-1994 event records.

Following up on my 28 September preservation notice and your pointer to the online 1994 report, I ask whether you hold the underlying excavation archive (site code, context sheets, photographs, finds inventory, records) for Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr, what searches were made, and whether anything has been destroyed or transferred, requesting a reply by 16 November 2026 and that nothing be destroyed meanwhile.

I followed up my 28 September preservation notice, asking Archaeology Data Service to confirm what records it holds on Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr, what searches were made, and whether anything has been destroyed or moved, by 16 November 2026.

We narrowed our earlier request to ask Mount Stuart for any 1870–1880 lease or sale of Great House Farm, 1870s rentals showing the occupier, and the December 1938 sale of the Bute interest at Llandough, and asked for a reply by 6 November 2026.

A newsletter promotes a community drop-in event and reports widespread postal delivery problems in Llandough, including a letter to Royal Mail detailing missed medical appointments and long delays, demanding an investigation.

I submit a supplement to request 00211557 seeking the original 1970s County Treasures inventory entry for Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr from the former South Glamorgan County Council, plus related survey sheets and amendment records.

I submit a narrowed request linked to 00211484 and 00211483 seeking village green VG41's 1970 registration records, 1958 planning committee minutes referencing a Mrs Buckler, and council works records on the adjoining land from 1955 to 1988.

I set a 30 October 2026 deadline for the outcome of the internal review of FOI 00210772, warn I may ask the ICO to consider the delay under section 50, and ask for a preservation hold on planning records for applications 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES.
HM Land Registry confirmed automated receipt of enquiry 261015-6844273 and gave standard timescales of five to twenty working days for a reply.
We acknowledge the message about titles Z084NQV/N610CGV, WA240304 and WA231076 and the 1983 first registration, repeating that assistance is limited to constituents who supply full contact details.

events.kind: Reply · Asked for a fee or clarification
events.text: We ask whether you have a claim number relating to your email of 28 September 2026 about the preservation notice for Great House Farm.
We confirm receipt of your correspondence about Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr and note we are dealing with a high volume of requests, so replies within 20 working days may be delayed.
We confirm that the 22 October council meeting will now be held remotely only, using the Zoom link already sent to you.
We confirm receipt of your new request about 1610 Herbert survey S7 and Cardiff MSS microfilm for Llandough-juxta-Penarth, and note that replies may be delayed due to demand.
We explain our search covered Great House Farm, Ty Mawr Farm, Llandough and related place names, included the earliest Cardiff Museum accession registers, and confirm no further search log is held.
We thank you for your message and ask you to direct any further queries to our colleague, while correcting the spelling of our archivist's name.

We answered your 48-item schedule on Great House Farm, confirming most items are either published on Archwilio or not held by the HER, and refusing to release change-log data as personal information under UK GDPR.

We are not answering general enquiries until January 2027, but research visits remain available by three weeks' advance booking at £20 per day, and reproduction or loan requests can still be processed.

I send the scheduled chase for the overdue internal review of FOI 00210772, requested 7 July 2026, and ask the council to suspend any disposal of related 1988 eviction, demolition, planning and Building Preservation Notice records pending the outcome.

I applied to HM Land Registry under Z084NQV/N610CGV for alteration of the register under Schedule 4 LRA 2002 and indemnity under Schedule 8, covering titles WA240304 (closed) and WA231076, focused on the 1983 first registration through 1987, restating earlier unanswered questions and adding new ones.

I ask under the Freedom of Information Act which items in Glamorgan land tax assessments DBJ/O/90-94 (1691–1707) cover Llandough-juxta-Penarth, and whether any record shows a 1667 999-year lease of Great House to the Williams family, distinct from Llandough-juxta-Cowbridge.
I ask for the substantive response to ATISN 26-0010 on retention and disposal schedules as soon as possible, particularly any covering Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr records from 1988-1996.

Following the reply on ATISN 27021, I ask Cadw to confirm whether any inventory, closure note or disposal schedule survives for the 1988 listing file, which successor or predecessor bodies might hold related material, and the recorded reason and date for any disposal decision.

I flagged that the Glamorgan XLVII.6 field book, plan and index, plus National Farm Survey and CWAEC records, must not be disposed of or weeded before location and physical-check status are confirmed, and asked for confirmation on retention schedules and missing items.

I pointed out that the 14 October reply only gave catalogue search links and did not answer the location request for the Glamorgan XLVII.6 field book, plan and index, and asked for series/item references, store location, physical-check status and the statutory deadline.

I requested, for two named hearth tax rolls (E 179/221/297 and E 179/221/294), which rotulet covers Llandough-juxta-Penarth, any householder names and hearth counts listed in finding aids, and digitisation or copying costs for that entry only.

I reiterate that information about my late father is not shielded in the way a living person's data would be, ask that FOI 1264/26 be read accordingly, and request preservation of liaison records on the 1988 possession and demolition.

I am asking BP p.l.c., BP Properties Ltd, the BP Pension Trust and any successors to preserve all records from 1969 to present relating to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, including litigation and demolition files, and I ask for the name of any external solicitors involved.

Ahead of the 22 October meeting, I ask that the outcome or a firm date for my open FOI and internal review requests be communicated beforehand, and I ask you to confirm that 1988-1992 planning records for refs 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES are being retained pending wider preservation enquiries.

I clarify, in plain terms, the military language used in my 13 October email, confirming it expressed frustration and political opinion rather than any threat, and state that all the formal requests in that email still stand.

I object to the council's decision to hold the 22 October meeting remotely only, ask it to reconsider, and pose five questions about who decided this, when, and what consideration was given to public access.

I open a new FOI request, separate from earlier ones, asking whether the 1610 Herbert survey S7 holds an entry for Great House in Llandough-juxta-Penarth, and whether Bute X.6(12) appears on the Cardiff MSS microfilm, with references.

I thank you for the catalogue links and ask you to confirm that no Bute Estate records relating to Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Great House, Daniel Thomas or John Williams have been reported missing, withdrawn or disposed of, and ask for any held information on the 1610 survey S7 or Bute X.6(12).
The family asks what search terms and systems were used to assess scope for FOI 2026-024, and whether predecessor records from the former National Museum of Wales or GGAT were included.
